extracted.intended_audience: pharmaceutical and plant protection product manufacturers, patent holders, IP professionals, national patent offices and EU policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the legal requirements, scope, duration, and procedural rules for obtaining and operating supplementary protection certificates (SPCs) for medicinal and plant protection products in the EU, including proposed reforms (centralised procedure, unitary SPCs) and the manufacturing waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — applicable product types
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary protection certificates (SPCs) apply to specific pharmaceutical and plant protection products that have been authorised by regulatory authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPCs are an intellectual property right that serve as an extension to a patent right and are specifically intended for medicinal and plant protection products that obtained regulatory authorisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — compensation for regulatory delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary protection certificates aim to offset the loss of patent protection for pharmaceutical and plant protection products that occurs due to the compulsory lengthy testing and clinical trials required prior to obtaining regulatory marketing approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPCs are intended to provide sufficient protection in the interest of public health and to encourage innovation in these areas by compensating for time lost during the pre-marketing authorisation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration — maximum SPC term
rubrics_metrics.description: An SPC can extend a patent right for a maximum of five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basic cap on SPC extension is five years (subject to the paediatric extension described separately).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paediatric extension — six-month additional term and PIP requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A six-month additional extension is available in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006 if the SPC relates to a medicinal product for children for which data has been submitted according to a Paediatric Investigation Plan (PIP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIPs are required to support the authorisation of medicines for children and ensure sufficient data is collected on effects in children; the extra six months compensates for additional clinical trials and testing PIPs require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal framework — governing EU regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The creation and operation of SPCs are governed by EU legislation, notably Council Regulation (EC) No 469/2009 (codifying Council Regulation (EEC) No 1768/92) for medicinal products and Regulation (EC) No 1610/96 for plant protection products, and amendments such as Regulation (EU) 2019/933.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists and links the principal regulations, amendments, impact assessments and related documents forming the legal basis for SPCs in the EU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirement — marketing authorisation / authorisation linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: SPCs apply to products that have been authorised by regulatory authorities; proposals further specify availability where the basic patent is a European patent and the product has a market authorisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A regulatory marketing authorisation for the specific product is a precondition for SPC protection; reforms reiterate the link between the patent basis (European or unitary) and the existence of a market authorisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary patent interaction — national SPCs and unitary SPCs
rubrics_metrics.description: National SPCs can be granted on the basis of a unitary patent; proposals confirm this and (once adopted) will enable extension of a unitary patent by a unitary SPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2012 patent package did not provide for a unitary SPC; the April 2023 proposals address treatment of unitary patents and envisage both national SPCs based on unitary patents and the creation of a unitary SPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralised procedure proposal and EUIPO role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposed a comprehensive reform including a new centralised procedure for granting national SPCs (available where the basic patent is a European patent and the product has a market authorisation) to be implemented by the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) with close involvement of national examiners experienced in SPC matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The centralised procedure is intended to reduce costs and administrative burden, improve legal certainty and transparency; national examiners will remain closely involved to preserve substantive expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined application mechanism (unitary + national SPCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposal it will be possible to file a single ‘combined application’, resulting in the granting of a unitary SPC and of national SPCs for additional Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This option is available where the basic patent has unitary effect and aims to simplify filings across multiple Member States and create a unitary SPC in a single process.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPC manufacturing waiver — export and stockpiling exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation (EU) 2019/933 entitles EU-based companies to manufacture a generic or biosimilar version of an SPC-protected medicine during the term of the certificate if done either for the purpose of exporting to a non-EU market, or for stockpiling during the final 6 months of an SPC ahead of entry into the EU market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The waiver aims to remove competitive disadvantages faced by EU-based manufacturers compared to non-EU manufacturers and to strike a balance between protecting innovators and allowing EU-based generics/biosimilars to compete globally; the waiver is limited to specified purposes (export or final-6-month stockpiling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy objectives of reform
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed SPC reform aims at reducing costs and administrative burden, and improving legal certainty and transparency in SPC granting and management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reform proposals are supported by impact assessments, studies and public consultation evidence and are presented as essentially procedural adjustments to the current regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and impact assessment references
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions and proposals on SPCs are accompanied by impact assessments, studies and summaries (e.g., Max Planck Institute studies, Copenhagen Economics, Charles Rivers Associates, and other economic and legal analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These studies inform policy choices on unified SPC systems, economic impacts of SPCs and exemption provisions; the page links to impact assessments, annexes, summaries and consultation results to support reform rationale.
